transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, thanks. Well, what really brought me in is that my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore. 

I work as a jeweler, and lately, when I'm sitting at the bench, I just jump from thing to thing. Like, I'll go from checking a customer email, to looking at a saw mark on a piece of metal, to getting distracted by some random noise outside... and then I realize I’ve completely lost track of the whole work order. It's just getting really hard to do my job right now, and I need to figure out what's going on.
When did you first start noticing this difficulty staying focused?

Well, it started right after this jewelry show... I won an award there, actually. Right after that, I just got into this really wired, out-of-control stretch. That whole thing went on for about two weeks.
During that two-week wired stretch, did you need less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Yeah, that's exactly what happened. For a while there, I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night. But I wasn't tired at all. I'd wake up completely clear-headed and just... really excited to get going. I'd be at my bench cutting stones or posting new designs online way before sunrise.
Did you need to be hospitalized during that two-week period because of how wired or out of control you felt?
No, I didn't go to the hospital or anything like that. I just... I stayed home and worked. I mean, I felt pretty out of control, but I didn't end up needing to be hospitalized.
Have you ever felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day, during a distinct period of your life?

Yeah, actually. These past couple weeks have been pretty rough. I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling... it's just like the shine has gone out of everything. I've even caught myself crying in my truck before opening up the shop. It's been pretty much every day lately.
How long has this current period of feeling depressed lasted?
I'd say... it's been about a month now. That depressed, kind of guilty feeling has just been hanging over me the whole time.
During this depressed period, have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you would normally enjoy?

Not really, no. I mean, I still want to do the things I usually like. I still enjoy working on my metals and, you know, messing around with the stones in the shop. I just feel really heavy and down while I'm doing it. But I haven't lost interest in the actual stuff, if that makes sense.
During this month of feeling depressed, how has your sleep been compared with your usual sleep?

It's been pretty bad, honestly. Even when I get in bed at a normal hour now, I just toss and turn. I keep waking up way before dawn, just laying there thinking about this missed delivery at the shop. And when I finally drag myself out of bed, I don't feel rested at all.
During this depressed period, have you felt noticeably less energetic than usual nearly every day?

Yeah, definitely. I just feel so drained. My arms feel like lead when I'm sitting at the bench. Even doing simple stuff, like polishing a setting or carrying a tray of stones, it just completely wipes me out. And resting doesn't seem to help, you know? Like, a full night off doesn't fix it. I'm just exhausted all the time.

Distractibility and difficulty sustaining attention during the period
Depressed, heavy, hollow mood nearly every day for approximately one month
Insomnia with early-morning awakening and nonrestorative sleep
Marked fatigue and low energy nearly every day
Difficulty tracking work orders and completing jewelry work
Occupational functioning has become significantly harder

additional_requirements: No hospitalization was required during the elevated/wired period
